en.title: Kit Harington's Sydney Carton Arrives: A Tale of Two Cities Trailer Drops
en.summary: The classic Dickensian drama gets a gritty, star-studded adaptation for MGM+. Prepare for forbidden love and revolutionary fervor as the new trailer unveils the stakes.
en.body:
The sands of time are shifting, and Charles Dickens' enduring masterpiece, **A Tale of Two Cities**, is poised for a dramatic resurgence. A new trailer has just landed, offering a tantalizing glimpse into the upcoming four-part miniseries set to stream on MGM+ starting September 6. This co-production with the BBC, featuring **Kit Harington** in a pivotal role, promises a fresh, perhaps grittier, take on the timeless story of revolution, sacrifice, and enduring love.

Set against the backdrop of the French Revolution, the series casts **Kit Harington** as Sydney Carton, a dissolute but brilliant barrister. His path becomes inextricably linked with that of Charles Darnay (**François Civil**), a French aristocrat living in England under an assumed name, who is arrested for treason. Darnay's story intertwons with Lucie Manette (**Mirren Mack**), a young woman who believes her father, Dr. Manette, long presumed dead, is still alive. Lucie seeks Darnay's help to locate her father, inadvertently setting in motion a complex love triangle that will test the limits of loyalty and courage.

The trailer highlights the stark contrasts that define Dickens' novel – the "best of times" juxtaposed with the "worst of times." It showcases the opulent yet precarious world of the French aristocracy alongside the simmering rage of the revolutionaries. **Harington**, known for his iconic role as Jon Snow in **Game of Thrones**, brings a brooding intensity to Sydney Carton, a character whose self-destructive tendencies mask a profound capacity for heroism. The visual style hints at a production that respects the source material's historical context while infusing it with contemporary pacing and cinematic flair, aiming to resonate with a modern audience accustomed to serialized drama.

## A Tale of Two Cities: Why This Adaptation Matters

For fans of classic literature and compelling historical drama, this new adaptation arrives as a significant event. Dickens' **A Tale of Two Cities** remains one of the most widely read and studied novels in the English language, its themes of social injustice, redemption, and the human cost of political upheaval are as relevant today as they were in 1859. The casting of **Kit Harington**, a beloved figure from a generation-defining television series, immediately elevates the project's profile, drawing in viewers who might not typically seek out period dramas. The choice to place the series on MGM+, a newer streaming service, also signals an ambition to capture a dedicated audience looking for quality, character-driven content beyond the mainstream.

This isn't just another Dickens adaptation; it's an opportunity to re-examine a classic through a modern lens, potentially bringing new depth to beloved characters and reimagining familiar narrative arcs for a binge-watching generation. The success of this miniseries could pave the way for further ambitious literary adaptations on the platform, making it a crucial release for both the network and fans of serialized storytelling.

## What's Next

The four-part miniseries **A Tale of Two Cities** premieres on MGM+ on September 6. Viewers can expect a faithful yet dynamic interpretation of Dickens' celebrated novel, with the trailer promising intense drama, emotional depth, and a powerful exploration of one of literature's most iconic narratives. Keep an eye out for early reviews and audience reactions as the premiere date approaches.

content_raw: The winter of our despair continues in the trailer for the new version of Charles Dickens’ A Tale Of Two Cities . Typically the stuff of Masterpiece Theater , this co-production with the BBC will be slumming it on the newish streaming service MGM+, which is owned by Amazon but isn’t Prime Video. Game Of Thrones ’ Kit Harrington stars as Sydney Carton, the unpredictable young barrister charged with defending Charles Darnay (François Civil), a messenger arrested for treason after bringing word to Lucie Manette (Mirren Mack) that her long-thought-dead father was still alive. Lucie hires Sydney in hopes that Darnay can lead them to dear dad but starts a love triangle that results in all that best of times, worst of times stuff. Frankly, this should come as no surprise to the esteemed readers of The A.V. Club , who no doubt stayed awake in A.P. English long enough to get the gist of Dickens’ revolutionary novel.  The four-part miniseries probably won’t help you write that term paper or pass midterms, but it does begin streaming on MGM+ on September 6.
